陸.meaning: A fish is tired of water. It plants a <part>pennant</part> on a heap of <part>soil</part>, grows two wobbly <part>legs</part> and waddles up the beach to claim it while the seagulls stare. For the first time ever, a fish has reached <kanji>land</kanji>.
陸.on: Behind it lies the <sound>ree</sound>f it left, and above it a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo shouts the news.
陸.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps its cousin, a <sound>ca</sound>rp, watching it climb a hill.

離.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> gets one tail feather caught in an <part>animal trap</part>. She doesn't panic: she wiggles, pops the feather loose and flies off, leaving it behind in the jaws. Birds know just how to <kanji>detach</kanji>.
離.on: She lands on a coral <sound>ree</sound>f far out at sea, as far from traps as she can get.
離.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' she laughs, nibbling a crumb of <sound>na</sound>an, miles away from that trap.

脱.meaning: A cheeky <part>imp</part> sneaks out under the full <part>moon</part> for a midnight swim. Off come his boots, his hat and his tiny striped socks, flung into the reeds one by one. Only an owl watches him <kanji>undress</kanji>.
脱.on: A gang of frogs plays <sound>darts</sound> on the bank, using his hat as the board.
脱.kun: He leaves the rest of his clothes folded in a cosy <sound>noo</sound>k of an old tree.

島.meaning: A huge <part>bird</part> grows tired over the ocean and lands on a lonely <part>mountain</part> poking out of the waves. It nests there so long that grass grows on its back and crabs move into its feathers. Sailors now mark it on maps as an <kanji>island</kanji>.
島.on: The only thing ever seen moving is one giant <sound>toe</sound>, wiggling at the shoreline.
島.kun: A sailor's <sound>shi</sound>eld washes up on the shore, and a lla<sound>ma</sound> uses it as a sledge to slide down the bird's feathery back.

静.meaning: Two brothers <part>contend</part> all day over the TV remote, shouting and wrestling. Then their mum paints the playroom a soft <part>blue</part>, and the moment they walk in they yawn, sit down and start whispering. Now it's always <kanji>quiet</kanji>.
静.on: She keeps the remote locked in a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe, just in case.
静.kun: They count <sound>shee</sound>p, then <sound>zu</sound>cchinis, until they both drop off.

筋.meaning: Every night under the <part>moon</part>, a panda curls a barbell made of <part>bamboo</part> with a melon tied to each end, flexing one <part>muscle</part> after another in the pond. The other pandas just eat their bamboo. He has turned himself into pure <kanji>muscle</kanji>.
筋.on: A <sound>kin</sound>gfisher dives for the fish he scares out of the pond with every grunt.
筋.kun: After training he eats <sound>su</sound>shi in the back of a <sound>jee</sound>p, every sinew aching.

益.meaning: At the school fair, a goat with stubby <part>horns</part> licks clean <part>one</part> <part>dish</part> after another, all <part>eight</part> of them. The washing-up team cheers: no scrubbing tonight. Everybody gets the <kanji>benefit</kanji>.
益.on: An <sound>ech</sound>idna rolls under the table and polishes the dishes dry with its spikes.
益.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, more!' bleats the goat, and the pile of clean dishes keeps on increasing.

羽.meaning: A snowman wants to fly, so he sticks chips of <part>ice</part> in neat rows down both arms, like wings. He flaps, hops and lifts one inch off the ground before they melt. Next time, he'll borrow some real <kanji>feathers</kanji>.
羽.on: He cheers himself up with a hot bowl of <sound>u</sound>don, which melts his arms a bit more.
羽.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' honks a goose, catching his falling ice in a <sound>ne</sound>t.
